```{r}
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
```


```{r}
ssp1 <- rast("data/wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_MRI-ESM2-0_ssp126_2081-2100.tif")
ssp5 <- rast("data/wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_MRI-ESM2-0_ssp585_2081-2100.tif")
plot(ssp5[[1]])
```

```{r}
world_cities <- read_csv("data/World_Cities.csv")
names(world_cities)
head(world_cities)
```

```{r}
#筛选Japan主要城市
japan_cities <- world_cities %>%
  filter(CNTRY_NAME == "Japan")
```

```{r}
# Create spatial points using Web Mercator
japan_sf <- st_as_sf(
  japan_cities,
  coords = c("X", "Y"),
  crs = 3857
)

japan_sf <- st_transform(japan_sf, 4326)

print(japan_sf)
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = japan_sf, color = "red", size = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Major Cities in Japan")
```

```{r}
#提取 sf 空间对象中各个城市的坐标
st_coordinates(japan_sf)

japan_sf$lon <- st_coordinates(japan_sf)[, 1]
japan_sf$lat <- st_coordinates(japan_sf)[, 2]

#从 japan_sf 空间数据中移除几何信息，只保留城市名称、人口、经度和纬度
japan_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(CITY_NAME, POP, lon, lat)
```

```{r}
#检查栅格坐标系
st_crs(japan_sf)
crs(ssp5)
compareGeom(ssp1, ssp5)
```

```{r}
japan_vect <- vect(japan_sf)

japan_vect <- project(
  japan_vect,
  crs(ssp1)
)
```

```{r}
#Extract temperature values at city locations
temp_ssp1 <- terra::extract(ssp1, japan_vect)
temp_ssp5 <- terra::extract(ssp5, japan_vect)
head(temp_ssp1)
head(temp_ssp5)
```

```{r}
# Calculate annual mean maximum temperature for SSP1
ssp1_mean <- rowMeans(temp_ssp1[, -1], na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate annual mean maximum temperature for SSP5
ssp5_mean <- rowMeans(temp_ssp5[, -1], na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Create a data frame for temperature comparison
results <- data.frame(
  City = japan_sf$CITY_NAME,
  SSP1 = ssp1_mean,
  SSP5 = ssp5_mean
)

# Calculate temperature differences between scenarios
results <- results %>%
  mutate(
    Difference = SSP5 - SSP1
  )

# Display the results
print(results)
```

```{r}
# Sort cities by temperature difference
results_sorted <- results %>%
  arrange(desc(Difference))

# Create the plot
p <- ggplot(
  results_sorted,
  aes(
    x = reorder(City, Difference),
    y = Difference
  )
) +

  # Draw horizontal bars
  geom_col(
    fill = "steelblue",
    width = 0.7
  ) +

  # Add temperature difference labels
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f°C", Difference)),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.5
  ) +

  # Flip x and y axes
  coord_flip() +

  # Set axis limits
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 3.5),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  # Add titles and labels
  labs(
    title = "Projected Temperature Difference by City",
    subtitle = "SSP5-8.5 minus SSP1-2.6 | Japan, 2081–2100",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Temperature Difference (°C)",
    caption = "Source: WorldClim CMIP6 climate projections"
  ) +

  # Apply a clean theme
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  # Customise the appearance
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 15
    ),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      colour = "grey50"
    )
  )

# Display the plot
print(p)
```

```{r}
# Descriptive statistics for SSP1
ssp1_stats <- results %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(SSP1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(SSP1, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(SSP1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min = min(SSP1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(SSP1, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = IQR(SSP1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Descriptive statistics for SSP5
ssp5_stats <- results %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(SSP5, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(SSP5, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(SSP5, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min = min(SSP5, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(SSP5, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = IQR(SSP5, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(ssp1_stats)
print(ssp5_stats)
```

```{r}
# Add scenario labels
ssp1_stats$Scenario <- "SSP1-2.6"
ssp5_stats$Scenario <- "SSP5-8.5"

# Combine descriptive statistics
summary_table <- bind_rows(
  ssp1_stats,
  ssp5_stats
) %>%
  select(Scenario, everything())

print(summary_table)
```

```{r}
# Convert statistics to long format
stats_long <- summary_table %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Mean, Median, SD, Min, Max, IQR),
    names_to = "Statistic",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Plot descriptive statistics
ggplot(stats_long,
       aes(x = Statistic, y = Value, fill = Scenario)) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "SSP1-2.6" = "steelblue",
      "SSP5-8.5" = "tomato"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Descriptive Statistics of Projected Temperature",
    subtitle = "Japanese Cities, 2081–2100",
    x = "Statistic",
    y = "Temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Scenario"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot(stats_long,
       aes(x = Scenario, y = Value, fill = Scenario)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Statistic,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "SSP1-2.6" = "steelblue",
      "SSP5-8.5" = "tomato"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Descriptive Statistics",
    subtitle = "SSP1-2.6 vs SSP5-8.5 | Japan, 2081–2100",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Value (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}

```


```{r}

# Crop raster data to Japan's bounding box

jp_ssp5_crop <- terra::crop(ssp5, jp_vect)
```

## Temporal Analysis of Projected Temperatures

The projected monthly maximum temperatures in Japan exhibit a clear seasonal pattern under both SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 during 2081–2100. Temperatures increase from winter to summer, reaching their highest levels in August before declining towards December.

SSP5-8.5 consistently produces higher projected temperatures than SSP1-2.6 throughout the year. However, the magnitude of the difference varies by month.

The largest difference occurs in October (approximately 3.27°C), while the smallest occurs in May (approximately 2.29°C). This indicates that the difference between climate scenarios is seasonally variable rather than constant.

Interestingly, the largest scenario difference does not coincide with the warmest month. These findings suggest that the seasonal pattern of projected temperature differences warrants further spatial investigation.

```{r}
# Calculate monthly spatial differences
jp_monthly_diff <- jp_ssp5 - jp_ssp1

# Rename layers using month abbreviations
names(jp_monthly_diff) <- month.abb

# Display all monthly difference maps
plot(
  jp_monthly_diff,
  main = paste("Temperature Difference -", month.abb)
)
```

```{r using the same colour scale}
# Find the global range across all 12 months
monthly_range <- terra::global(
  jp_monthly_diff,
  "range",
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Determine common colour limits
common_min <- min(monthly_range[, 1])
common_max <- max(monthly_range[, 2])

# Plot maps using the same colour scale
plot(
  jp_monthly_diff,
  range = c(common_min, common_max),
  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd"),
  main = month.abb
)
```

## How similar are the spatial patterns of temperature differences across different months?

```{r}
# Convert monthly raster differences into a data frame
diff_values <- terra::values(
  jp_monthly_diff,
  na.rm = FALSE
)

# Calculate Pearson correlations between all months
cor_matrix <- cor(
  diff_values,
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

# Display the correlation matrix
round(cor_matrix, 3)
```

```{r}
# Convert correlation matrix to long format
cor_df <- as.data.frame(cor_matrix)

cor_df$Month1 <- rownames(cor_df)

cor_long <- cor_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Month1,
    names_to = "Month2",
    values_to = "Correlation"
  )

# Set month order
cor_long$Month1 <- factor(
  cor_long$Month1,
  levels = month.abb
)

cor_long$Month2 <- factor(
  cor_long$Month2,
  levels = month.abb
)

# Plot correlation heatmap
ggplot(
  cor_long,
  aes(x = Month1, y = Month2, fill = Correlation)
) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Correlation)),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "firebrick",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Spatial Correlation of Monthly Temperature Differences",
    subtitle = "SSP5-8.5 minus SSP1-2.6 | Japan, 2081–2100",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Month",
    fill = "Pearson r"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

## Spatial Correlation of Monthly Temperature Differences

Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between monthly raster layers to assess the similarity of spatial patterns in projected temperature differences between SSP5-8.5 and SSP1-2.6.

All pairwise monthly correlations were positive, ranging from approximately 0.26 to 0.98. The strongest correlation was observed between November and December (r = 0.98), indicating highly similar spatial patterns. Strong correlations were also found between February and December (r = 0.97) and between June and August (r = 0.93).

In contrast, April and July showed the weakest correlation (r = 0.26), suggesting that the geographical distribution of temperature differences varies substantially between these months.

Overall, the results indicate that the spatial patterns of projected temperature differences are partly persistent but also exhibit seasonal variation. Further spatial analysis is needed to identify the geographical structure of these differences and assess spatial clustering.

```{r Geographical Gradients in Projected Temperature Differences}
# Extract raster values and coordinates for all valid cells
pixel_data <- as.data.frame(
  jp_monthly_diff,
  xy = TRUE,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Inspect the first six rows
head(pixel_data)

nrow(pixel_data)
```

```{r}
# January: latitude and temperature difference
cor(pixel_data$y, pixel_data$Jan)

# January: longitude and temperature difference
cor(pixel_data$x, pixel_data$Jan)

# July: latitude and temperature difference
cor(pixel_data$y, pixel_data$Jul)

# July: longitude and temperature difference
cor(pixel_data$x, pixel_data$Jul)
```


```{r}
# Calculate correlations for all 12 months
```

```{r}
library(tidyr)

# Reshape correlation results
monthly_cor_long <- monthly_cor %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Latitude, Longitude),
    names_to = "Coordinate",
    values_to = "Correlation"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = month.abb))

# Plot monthly correlation coefficients
ggplot(
  monthly_cor_long,
  aes(x = Month, y = Correlation,
      colour = Coordinate, group = Coordinate)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Correlation Between Location and Temperature Difference",
    subtitle = "Pixel-level analysis | Japan, 2081–2100",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Pearson Correlation",
    colour = "Coordinate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

```{r PCA}
# Convert raster-cell coordinates into spatial points
pixel_sf <- st_as_sf(
  pixel_data,
  coords = c("x", "y"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

# Use an Azimuthal Equidistant projection centred on Japan
japan_crs <- paste(
  "+proj=aeqd",
  "+lat_0=36",
  "+lon_0=138",
  "+datum=WGS84",
  "+units=m",
  "+no_defs"
)

pixel_projected <- st_transform(pixel_sf, japan_crs)

# Extract projected coordinates in kilometres
coords_km <- st_coordinates(pixel_projected) / 1000

pixel_data$X_km <- coords_km[, 1]
pixel_data$Y_km <- coords_km[, 2]

head(pixel_data[, c("x", "y", "X_km", "Y_km")])
```

```{r}
# Perform PCA on projected spatial coordinates
pca_axis <- prcomp(
  pixel_data[, c("X_km", "Y_km")],
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

# Examine explained variance
summary(pca_axis)

# Examine the direction of the main axis
pca_axis$rotation
```

```{r}
# Extract PCA coordinates
axis_scores <- predict(pca_axis)

pixel_data$PC1 <- axis_scores[, 1]
pixel_data$PC2 <- axis_scores[, 2]

# Orient PC1 so that larger values point northeast
if (cor(pixel_data$PC1, pixel_data$Y_km) < 0) {
  pixel_data$PC1 <- -pixel_data$PC1
  pixel_data$PC2 <- -pixel_data$PC2
}

# Set southwest end of the main axis to zero
pixel_data$Axis_km <- pixel_data$PC1 - min(pixel_data$PC1)

# Inspect the result
head(pixel_data[, c("X_km", "Y_km", "Axis_km", "Jan")])
```

```{r}
# Plot raster-cell positions coloured by main-axis distance
ggplot(pixel_data, aes(x = X_km, y = Y_km)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = Axis_km),
    size = 0.4,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    option = "plasma",
    name = "Axis distance (km)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Japan's Main Geographical Axis",
    subtitle = "PCA-derived axis based on raster-cell locations",
    x = "Projected Easting (km)",
    y = "Projected Northing (km)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Calculate temperature difference gradients along Japan's main axis
axis_gradient <- data.frame(
  Month = month.abb,
  Gradient = sapply(
    month.abb,
    function(m) {

      # Fit linear regression along the main axis
      model <- lm(
        pixel_data[[m]] ~ pixel_data$Axis_km
      )

      # Convert slope to °C per 100 km
      unname(coef(model)[2]) * 100
    }
  )
)

# Set chronological month order
axis_gradient$Month <- factor(
  axis_gradient$Month,
  levels = month.abb
)

print(axis_gradient)
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  axis_gradient,
  aes(x = Month, y = Gradient, group = 1)
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    colour = "steelblue",
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    colour = "firebrick",
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Temperature Difference Gradient Along Japan's Main Axis",
    subtitle = "SSP5-8.5 minus SSP1-2.6 | 2081–2100",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Main-axis Gradient (°C / 100 km)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

```{r}
# Calculate R-squared for each monthly main-axis regression
axis_r2 <- sapply(
  month.abb,
  function(m) {
    model <- lm(
      pixel_data[[m]] ~ pixel_data$Axis_km
    )

    summary(model)$r.squared
  }
)

# Combine gradient and model explanatory power
axis_gradient$R_squared <- unname(axis_r2)

print(axis_gradient)
```

```{r}
# Plot monthly R-squared values
ggplot(axis_gradient,
       aes(x = Month, y = R_squared, group = 1)) +

  # Add a line connecting monthly values
  geom_line(
    colour = "steelblue",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  # Add points for each month
  geom_point(
    colour = "firebrick",
    size = 3
  ) +

  # Display R-squared values above points
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", R_squared)),
    vjust = -0.8,
    size = 3.5
  ) +

  # Set y-axis limits
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Seasonal Variation in Main-Axis Model R²",
    subtitle = "Japan | SSP5-8.5 minus SSP1-2.6 | 2081–2100",
    x = "Month",
    y = expression(R^2)
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## Spatial Gradient Analysis

To quantify the spatial patterns observed in the temperature difference maps, a spatial gradient analysis was conducted using raster-cell data across Japan. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to projected geographical coordinates to identify the country's main southwest-to-northeast axis. Linear regression was then used to estimate changes in projected temperature differences between SSP5-8.5 and SSP1-2.6 along this axis.

The results revealed positive spatial gradients in all twelve months, indicating that projected temperature differences generally increased from southwestern to northeastern Japan.

The strength of this gradient varied seasonally. December exhibited the strongest gradient (0.067°C per 100 km), followed by February (0.058°C per 100 km) and November (0.049°C per 100 km). In contrast, April showed the weakest gradient (0.011°C per 100 km).

The explanatory power of the linear models also varied substantially. The highest R² values were observed in December (0.928) and November (0.915), indicating that the main-axis trend accounted for more than 91% of the spatial variation in projected temperature differences during these months. April had the lowest R² (0.220), suggesting a more complex spatial pattern that could not be adequately represented by a simple linear gradient.

Overall, the analysis demonstrates a persistent but seasonally variable southwest-to-northeast gradient in projected temperature differences across Japan. The results provide quantitative support for the spatial patterns identified through visual interpretation of the raster maps.
